ColorPicker

The ColorPicker control allows users to edit the red, green and blue values of a color. It shows the original color alongside the current color, so changes can be previewed before they are saved.

Properties and Methods

  • ColorValue / OriginalColor: ColorValue is the color being edited. OriginalColor is the value that Cancel will restore. Alpha is preserved but cannot be edited here.
  • BeginEdit(Color): Sets the starting color and resets the edit state. Attaching the picker also records its starting color.
  • TrySetHex(string): Sets a color from six hex digits, with or without a leading #. Returns false if the input is invalid.
  • Commit() / Cancel(): Commit accepts the current color as the new starting value. Cancel restores the original color. Each method calls its corresponding event.
  • ColorChanged / Confirmed / Cancelled: Action<Color> events for previewing changes and handling completion.

C# Example

Create the control and add it to the page's Children or the window's Elements collection. The Controls Overview lists the namespaces used by these examples.

MXML Example

App refers to the SettingsModel backend from the Data Binding Guide. Register it with page.BackendObjects.Add("App", model) before compiling.

Output Example

Keyboard Controls

  • Up / Down: Choose R, G or B.
  • Left / Right; Shift+Left / Right: Adjust by one with bounded repeat acceleration; Shift uses ten.
  • Home / End, digits: Set 0/255 or type a channel value.
  • Enter / Escape: Commit / cancel. The host decides whether the dialog closes.

Notes

RgbColorPicker is another name for the same control. You can use either name in C# or MXML.

Commit and Cancel do not close the control. If you are using a popup, close or dispose its handle from the Confirmed and Cancelled callbacks.

The common position, color, visibility and lifetime settings are inherited from UIElement. While attached to a running window, update the control on the UI thread.
